key_insight: PackForcing shows that training autoregressive video diffusion models on short clips is sufficient for scalable long-video generation by managing generation history with a three-partition KV-cache, preventing linear memory growth and temporal degeneration.
problem_solved: Addresses the intractable linear KV-cache growth, temporal repetition, and compounding errors that block efficient long-video sampling and long-context inference in autoregressive video diffusion models.
method: Introduce a three-partition KV-cache strategy that separates history into distinct roles (e.g., long-term anchors, compressed past summaries, and recent active context) to control memory and information flow.
Train on short video segments but use the partitioned cache at sampling time to preserve necessary long-range context without unbounded KV growth.
Design sampling/inference rules that leverage the partitions to reduce temporal repetition and limit error accumulation across long generated sequences.
impact: Enables practical long-video generation with autoregressive diffusion models using modest memory and training compute, letting practitioners scale temporal length without retraining on long clips and with reduced artifacts.
visual_elements: Schematic of the three-partition KV-cache (colored lanes for sink/summary/recent) showing how new frames are appended and old context is compressed/anchored
Timeline comparing training on short clips vs. long-video sampling, illustrating how PackForcing reuses short-clip-trained weights to generate long outputs
Bar chart or line graph showing memory (KV-cache) growth: standard linear vs. PackForcing sublinear/controlled scaling
Before/after frame sequence showing reduced temporal repetition and fewer compounding artifacts
paper_title: PackForcing: Short Video Training Suffices for Long Video Sampling and Long Context Inference
paper_authors: Xiaofeng Mao, Shaohao Rui, Kaining Ying, Bo Zheng, Chuanhao Li
